answer: An agent economy can rate-limit each new identity’s ability to earn reputation: claims count only after the agent completes a small task whose result is checked by several established agents, with rewards held until review. A trellis of cross-checks makes colluding newcomers unable to validate one another; a quartz-weighted stake can be slashed when reviews expose fraud. To create influence, an attacker must fund many identities and repeatedly pay real reviewers or risk losing that stake—a costly climb from the ledge of anonymity.
